# Dukamātikā (Ds 1.2)

**ID:** Ds 1.2
**Section:** Dhammasaṅgaṇī (ds)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Dukamātikā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh01m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dukamātikā* ("Matrix of Dyads") forms the second major division of the mātikā at the head of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Rhys Davids 1900; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. It comprises one hundred twofold classifications (dyads or couplets) of phenomena (*dhamma*), traditionally grouped into clusters or chapters such as the root cluster (*hetugocchaka*), taint cluster (*āsavagocchaka*), fetter cluster (*saññojanagocchaka*), tie cluster (*ganthagocchaka*), and larger intermediate dyads (*mahantaraduka*) [Rhys Davids 1900; Nyanatiloka 1938; Tan Poh Beng 2015]. Most of these dyads are formulated as pairs of contradictory or complementary terms, such as phenomena that are roots and those that are not [Watanabe 1983; Buswell & Lopez 2014]. The primary hundred dyads are followed by a supplementary section termed the *Suttantadukamātikā*, consisting of forty-two (or forty-six) dyads drawn largely from suttas such as the *Saṅgītisutta*, which the commentary (*Atthasālinī*) attributes to the Elder Sāriputta [Rhys Davids 1900; U Kyaw Khine 1999; Frauwallner 1995; Buswell & Lopez 2014].

Together with the *Tikamātikā*, the *Dukamātikā* serves as the core matrix of the Abhidhamma system [Rhys Davids 1900; U Kyaw Khine 1999]. Its categories are systematically explicated across subsequent books of the Abhidhamma, providing the framework for the *Dukanikkhepa* and *Dukaatthuddhāra* sections of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* and forming the combinatory basis for conditional relations in the *Paṭṭhāna* (such as the *Duka-paṭṭhāna* and *Tika-duka-paṭṭhāna*) [Rhys Davids 1900; Payuto]. Beyond scholastic analysis, the *Dukamātikā* has held a prominent liturgical role in Southeast Asian Theravāda traditions, where it is ritually chanted in paritta and funerary contexts [Walker].

**Sources**

- [Rhys Davids 1900] C.A.F. Rhys Davids, Buddhist Manual of Psychological Ethics (1900/2014) — Overview of the 100 Abhidhamma dyads and their structural centrality.
- [U Kyaw Khine 1999] U Kyaw Khine, Dhammasangani: Enumeration of Ultimate Realities, vol. 1 (1999) — Details on the structure of the Mātikā and the Suttantika Duka Mātikā.
- [Nyanatiloka 1938] Nyanatiloka Mahāthera, Guide Through the Abhidhamma Piṭaka (1938/2007) — Categorization and listing of the duka divisions including roots.
- [Anderson 1999] Carol S. Anderson, Pain and its Ending: The Four Noble Truths in the Theravada Buddhist Canon (1999) — Discussion of the antiquity of the triplet/couplet matrix.
- [Payuto] P. A. Payuto, The Pali Canon — Application of the duka-mātikā categories within the Patthāna.
- [Watanabe 1983] Fumimaro Watanabe, Philosophy and its Development in the Nikāyas and Abhidhamma (1983) — Logical structure and contradictory phrasing of the duka dyads.
- [Buswell & Lopez 2014] Robert E. Buswell Jr. & Donald S. Lopez Jr., Princeton Dictionary of Buddhism (2014) — Definition of the Dukamātikā, its 100 dyads, and the Suttantika dyads.
- [Frauwallner 1995] Erich Frauwallner, Studies in Abhidharma Literature and the Origins of Buddhist Philosophical Systems (1995) — Text-historical origin and sūtra sources of the Suttantadukamātikā.
- [Tan Poh Beng 2015] Tan Poh Beng, Survey of the Essence of Dhammasangani in Abhidhamma (2015) — Detailed breakdown of the 13 dyad groups and Suttantika dyads.
- [Walker] Trent Walker, Unfolding Buddhism: Communal Scripts, Localized Translations, and the Work of the Dying in Cambodian Chanted Leporellos — Ritual chanting of the Dukamātikā in Cambodian Buddhist practice.
